name: List Sort Binary Removal Lookup

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## List Sort Binary Removal Lookup Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

`ListSortState::remove_sorted_item` scans the whole sorted vector with `==` for the item a Remove/RemoveRange/Replace names: O(n) per removal. An item equal by `==` sorts equal, so it lies in the comparer-equal range that a binary search finds in O(log n); scanning only that range for `==` (falling back to the full scan when the item is not there, e.g. after an unannounced in-place mutation) finds it without the linear scan.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** binary search to the equal range before the equality scan.
**Allowed changes:** `remove_sorted_item` and its three call sites in `list_sort_state.rs` (to pass the comparer).
**Forbidden in this experiment:** refresh lookup, insert path, keyed sort.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Focused tests: `collections::tests::{sorting_windowing,window_responses,index_contract_harness,subset_operator_indexes,keyed_sort_positions,snapshot_diff_indexes}`; clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` (list-hot/insert-remove-sort) vs base. Pass: insert-remove-sort >=20% faster than after experiment 17.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

insert-remove-sort drops further (removal scan gone); memmoves remain.
